ownership_decision.invariant: An exposure review is an immutable record binding one release, its content hash and the digest of the text search holds; only the newest review of the newest release decides exposure.

boundary_decision.interaction: Publishing reads the search snapshot from Catalog, and Catalog reads the exposed set from Publishing, each through a function the composition root injects; neither imports the other.

domain_forces: Sharing a Skill and the catalog vouching for it are different promises, so exposure cannot follow from publishing.
A reviewer must approve exactly what readers will find, and nothing they did not see may ride on their approval.
implementation_design.decision: Publishing owns the review record, bound to the release and a digest of the searchable text; every public read asks Publishing for the exposed set and matches skill, version and digest in the same query, so a new release, a new upload, a re-enrichment or a governance change withdraws exposure on the next read.
invariants_preserved: Catalog owns the search projection and the catalog workspaces keep their exposure without reviews.
Registry owns Skill facts, takedowns, holds and redistribution verdicts.
rejected_alternatives: Reviews owned by Catalog: the reviewed thing is a release, which only Publishing has, and the architecture decision places reviews there.
A listed flag written into the search projection: an asynchronous refresh would let stale approvals stay public.

record.name: Publishing
record.responsibility: Owns who discloses what under which name: a creator's publisher namespace, the publications and Bundles in it, their immutable releases, and the operator reviews that expose a release to search.

approvals.scope: Publishing widens to Bundles and operator exposure reviews bound to a release and a search-text digest; Catalog and Publishing exchange exposure and snapshot facts through composition-root injection only
